newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities steady to higher.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended steady to higher in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said on Wednesday.

"The interbank rate was slightly lower today but there was little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields were slightly higher but bond prices were steady to slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.93/2.88 percent compared with Tuesday's yield of 2.90/2.85 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.72/2.67 percent against 2.70/2.65 percent.
Among bonds, April 1999 was unchanged from Tuesday's close of S$98.55/98.60 and September 2001 unchanged at S$96.35/96.45.
June 2003 ended at S$94.45/94.50 versus Tuesday's close of S$94.41/94.46.
The overnight interbank offered rate eased to 3-3/8 3-1/4 percent against Tuesday's 3-1/2 3-3/8 percent.
